raw_record.support_text: Hartman et al (cited) reported that hycanthone was a potent frameshift mutagen in Salmonella. This identifies hycanthone as a potent mutagen in a bacterial reverse-mutation (frameshift) assay.
raw_record.extra_details: Described as a potent frameshift mutagen in Salmonella; hycanthone is a thioxanthone metabolite of lucanthone tested clinically as an antischistosomal drug.

raw_record.support_text: The junctions between euchromatin and heterochromatin in D. melanogaster are stated to be the preferential sites of x-ray-, methyl methanesulfonate-, and UV-induced breaks as well as of sister-chromatid exchanges (citations 18, 19, 26, 27). This establishes that methyl methanesulfonate induces chromosome breaks/aberrations in Drosophila melanogaster neuroblasts.
raw_record.test_system: Drosophila melanogaster neuroblast cells (male and female)
raw_record.extra_details: The paper also notes that mei-9 and mei-41 mutants show extreme sensitivity to methyl methanesulfonate (citations 10, 12, 16) and that females show a higher frequency of methyl methanesulfonate-induced aberrations than males in wild-type flies (citations 17, 18, 27). Breaks preferentially occur at euchromatin-heterochromatic junctions. Methyl methanesulfonate is used as an inducing/clastogenic agent rather than tested in a bacterial system.

raw_record.support_text: The authors state they studied whether this antipsoriatic agent (psoralen, used here as 8-MOP) is a potent inducer of mitochondrial mutations in yeast in the same way as dithranol, coal tar extracts and methotrexate, and upon finding that this was the case (reference 20) they commenced psoralen + UVA treatment of patients.

raw_record.support_text: In a yeast-based drug screen, five compounds (pergolide mesylate, benzydamine HCl, otilonium bromide, trifluoperazine 2HCl, and sertraline HCl) were identified for their ability to suppress the defective respiratory phenotype of haploid Δaac1Δaac2 yeast expressing the Aac2p Met114Pro mutant. These drugs were effective in reducing mtDNA instability (petite formation) in the heteroallelic AAC2/aac2Met114Pro strain and in the heteroallelic strain carrying the Arg96His mutation equivalent to dominant ANT1 Arg80His.
raw_record.biological_test_system: Saccharomyces cerevisiae; W303-1B-derived; haploid Δaac1Δaac2 and heteroallelic AAC2/aac2Met114Pro and AAC2/aac2Arg96His strains
raw_record.extra_details: Benzydamine HCl reduced mtDNA instability in heteroallelic AAC2/aac2Met114Pro and AAC2/aac2Arg96His strains; not able to rescue the respiratory growth defect but rescued the oxidative defect of Aac2p Ala128Pro and Ser303Met mutants. Direction of result is suppression/reduction of mtDNA instability (protective). Concentration/dose not reported; yeast-screening context; no standard genotoxicity dose-response data given.

raw_record.support_text: In the presence of 1 mM GSH, treatment of L5178Y/TK+/- mouse lymphoma cells with 5-35 µg/ml methyl acrylate did not lead to mutagenicity: mean corrected mutant frequencies were between 49.9 and 98.5 per 10^6 cells versus 70.4 in the vehicle control, all below the calculated GEF-based threshold (126 + control = 196 mutant colonies per 10^6 cells), with no dose-related increase (linear-trend slope -1.79647, one-sided p = 0.953).
raw_record.biological_test_system: Mus musculus; L5178Y/TK+/- mouse lymphoma cell line
raw_record.extra_details: L5178Y/TK+/- mouse lymphoma mutation assay carried out in the presence of 1 mM GSH (co-treatment), which abrogated mutagenicity. Mean corrected mutant frequencies ranged 49.9-98.5 per 10^6 cells (control 70.4); highest dose 35 µg/ml gave MF 49.9 per 10^6 cells. All values below GEF threshold (126 + control = 196 mutant colonies per 10^6 cells). No dose-related increase by linear trend (slope -1.79647, one-sided p = 0.953). Small colonies (64-87, chromosome-mutation indicator) and large colonies (13-36, gene-mutation indicator) counted separately also showed no dose-related increase versus vehicle-control colonies (83 small, 17 large). Moore et al. 1988 had reported MA was mutagenic at 14 µg/ml in the same cell line in the absence of GSH.

raw_record.support_text: In studies on proflavine mutagenesis in bacteriophage T4, Ripley and Clarke (1986) observed a single hot spot for mutagenesis in which many different frameshifts were seen; the most frequent mutation was a +G frameshift producing a change in sequence from TTGTTAAA to TTGGTTAAA.
raw_record.extra_details: Forward-mutation assay in bacteriophage T4. Proflavine induced a single hot spot with a range of frameshifts; the most frequent was a +G frameshift (TTGTTAAA to TTGGTTAAA), with an overall symmetric pattern of mutations not fully predicted by the Streisinger misalignment model. The specific locus, dose, and exposure details are not given in this review window.

raw_record.support_text: SCC7 parental cells and cells that underwent five cycles of drug exposure (T5_resistant) were exposed to 4 nM SN-38 for 24 h, then processed for a γH2AX assay. raw_record.support_text: Kuroda et al. (2014) demonstrated that OTA also produces an increase in γ-H2AX expression and was capable of inducing double-strand breaks (DSBs) in DNA in a rat model. This is cited in a review discussing the mechanisms by which OTA can cause a clastogenic effect.

raw_record.support_text: CHO cells treated with 25 µM iodoacetic acid were assayed for genomic DNA damage by the single-cell gel electrophoresis (SCGE/comet) assay. The genotoxic damage produced by iodoacetic acid alone served as the baseline for comparison; cells treated concurrently with BHA showed a significant, concentration-dependent reduction in genotoxic damage relative to iodoacetic acid alone. Treatment conditions did not induce acute toxicity by the trypan blue vital dye method.

ZO-induced oxidative DNA damage was predicted by single-cell gel electrophoresis (comet assay). HCT116 cells treated with various concentrations (2.5, 5, and 10 µM) of ZO drastically increased DNA damage, shown as a comet in the single-cell gel electrophoresis assay; ZO significantly (P < .05) increased the percentage of DNA damage in HCT116 cells for 24 hours. Paragraph 51 specifies the comet assay was performed by alkaline gel electrophoresis (×20) in triplicate, values as mean ± SD, with significance P < .05 vs untreated control.
raw_record.biological_system: in vitro cells | Homo sapiens | HCT116
raw_record.extra_details: exposure_duration_or_schedule: 24 h treatment; significance: P < .05 vs untreated control with #, *, **, *** markers; all experiments in triplicate, values mean ± SD; no quantitative percentage value reported in supplied text; no metabolic activation mentioned.

raw_record.support_text: In rats fed the complete liquid diet vs Lab Blox, the overall elimination of acetaminophen decreased at all doses, due to a reduction in activity of all acetaminophen metabolism pathways including cytochrome P450-dependent conversion of acetaminophen to NAPQI (measured as mercapturate formation, Table 3). The protection from hepatotoxicity came from decreased production of the reactive metabolite NAPQI, with a ~50% decrease in this pathway. At the low dose (20 mg/kg) the apparent first-order rate constant K'_MA reflects the enzymatic Vmax/Km for P450-dependent NAPQI formation.
raw_record.assay_method_and_endpoint: Cytochrome P450-dependent conversion of acetaminophen to NAPQI estimated from mercapturate (NAPQI-GSH conjugate) formation and expressed as apparent first-order rate constant K'_MA (reflecting in-vivo Vmax/Km)
raw_record.biological_system: Rat (Rattus norvegicus), in vivo, hepatic metabolism; endpoint of CYP-dependent NAPQI formation
raw_record.exposure_and_mechanistic_conditions: Acetaminophen at low dose 20 mg/kg for K'_MA determination; diet comparison: complete liquid diet vs Lab Blox chow
raw_record.extra_details: Complete liquid diet reduced inducible P450-dependent NAPQI-formation pathway by about 50% vs Lab Blox; K'_MA values are given in Table 3 (not reproduced in this text window). Paper concern is hepatotoxicity, and these detoxification/activation parameters are interpreted as offsetting effects on susceptibility.

raw_record.support_text: Evidence from Figs. 12 and 13 and results for the sensitivity of RAD52, a mutant of Saccharomyces cerevisiae defective in repair of double strand breaks, confirms that anthramycin treatment of repair-proficient cells results in double strand breaks in DNA. The low ratio of single to double strand breaks (approximately 10:1) rules out coincident single strand breaks as the mechanism for double strand break formation, and the authors propose that persistent single strand breaks plus anthramycin lesions become double strand breaks as repair enzymes attempt to restore lesion-free duplex DNA.
raw_record.assay_method_and_endpoint: Detection of DNA double strand breaks in repair-proficient cells after anthramycin treatment, corroborated by sensitivity of the RAD52 double-strand-break-repair-defective mutant of Saccharomyces cerevisiae; ratio of single to double strand breaks approximately 10:1
raw_record.biological_system: Saccharomyces cerevisiae, repair-proficient cells versus a repair-proficient background compared against the RAD52 mutant defective in double strand break repair
raw_record.exposure_and_mechanistic_conditions: Anthramycin treatment of repair-proficient cells; no concentration, duration, or dose reported in the provided text
raw_record.extra_details: Ratio of single to double strand breaks approximately 10:1 was reported, argued to rule out coincident single strand breaks as the mechanism of double strand break formation. The molecular events leading to the double strand breaks are stated to be unknown; the authors propose repair-mediated conversion of persistent single strand breaks/lesions into double strand breaks. Assay details and concentrations are in Figs. 12-13, which are outside this window, so dose, method, and relevant non-anthramycin values are not provided.

raw_record.support_text: P450-mediated oxidative elimination of 1,3-DCP and related haloalkanes was evaluated in an automated headspace system using rat liver microsomes (0.72 mg microsomal protein/ml, pH 7.4, 37°C). Michaelis-Menten parameters fitted to the time courses gave Vmax = 30.3 nmol/h/mg microsomal protein and Km = 1.09 µM in the incubation medium (corresponding gas-phase Km = 3.2 ppm).
raw_record.assay_method_and_endpoint: Automated headspace system measuring oxidative (P450) clearance of haloalkane; Michaelis-Menten Vmax and Km fitted to headspace concentration-time courses after cofactor addition
raw_record.biological_system: Rat liver microsomes (cell-free subcellular fraction), Rattus norvegicus (Fischer-344 rat), 0.72 mg microsomal protein/ml, pH 7.4, 37°C
raw_record.exposure_and_mechanistic_conditions: Initial 1,3-DCP concentrations varied over a wide range; steady state reached in <10 min; P450 cofactor added typically between 30 and 50 min to initiate metabolism
raw_record.extra_details: Apparent Km = 1.09 µM in the incubation medium (corresponding gas-phase Km = 3.2 ppm, calculated from 1.09 µM × 24.45 M-1 with P = 8.4). Shallow slopes at high concentrations indicated saturable kinetics; steeper slopes at low concentrations indicated first-order kinetics. Across haloalkanes examined, predicted and experimental first-order P450 rates correlated with R2 = 0.79 (log-log).

raw_record.support_text: An adaptation of the dideoxynucleotide sequencing method was performed where DNA lesions in the template act as chain terminators. The analysis was performed on supercoiled plasmids extracted from R7000-treated bacteria; DNA replication was catalyzed by avian myeloblastosis virus (AMV) reverse transcriptase and reaction products were analyzed by sequencing gel electrophoresis. AMV reverse transcriptase termination on R7000-treated DNA occurred preferentially at the level of guanines in the template.

raw_record.endpoint_subtype: polymersse-arresting template lesions (R7000-DNA adducts) at guanine positions
raw_record.biological_system: DNA template assay | bacteria | supercoiled plasmids extracted from R7000-treated bacteria; AMV reverse transcriptase; comparison lane of dideoxy sequencing on untreated plasmid DNA
raw_record.response_value: reverse transcriptase termination preferentially at template guanines
raw_record.extra_details: positions of elongation arrests determined by comparison with dideoxy sequencing reactions using untreated plasmid DNA; evidence source: primary experimental result in supplied text.

raw_record.support_text: Frenkel and Chrzan (ref 200) incubated HeLa cells with stimulated polymorphonuclear leukocytes and found an increased level of 5-OHMe-dU, a dT oxidation product, in DNA isolated from the cells. Formation of this derivative could be prevented with catalase, indicating that H2O2 was the diffusible agent responsible for dT oxidation, with the authors speculating that oxidation of thymine was catalyzed by DNA-bound iron.
raw_record.assay_version: 5-OHMe-dU (thymidine oxidation product) measured in DNA isolated from treated cells
raw_record.biological_system: in vitro cells | Homo sapiens | HeLa
raw_record.extra_details: Focal entity role: H2O2 identified as the diffusible agent responsible for dT oxidation; source of the damage was stimulated polymorphonuclear leukocytes (neutrophils, ref 200). Catalase (positive/ablation control) prevented 5-OHMe-dU formation. Authors speculated oxidation catalyzed by DNA-bound iron. Evidence source: review narrative, secondary-source provenance (Frenkel and Chrzan, ref 200). Exposure was co-incubation of HeLa cells with stimulated PMN leukocytes; sampling time and numeric levels not reported.; compound_name: Hydrogen peroxide
